decision: Is the weak reused-heldout 16-frame physical-HIT action increment concentrated in logged-action support or post-HIT lifecycle strata, and how is each frozen probe miscalibrated?

hypotheses.H1_support_boundary: The full-minus-state-only HIT Brier delta may differ between actions that equal the reactive baseline and actions that provably differ from it. Raw logged propensity, shield-set size, and per-action counts are reported; latent mixture membership is not inferred.
hypotheses.H2_lifecycle_boundary: The full-minus-state-only HIT Brier delta may differ before the first physical HIT and at fixed elapsed-game-frame bands after a HIT. Every row and HIT remains in the factual episode and no post-HIT transition is relabeled terminal.
hypotheses.H3_calibration_boundary: Equal-width reliability bins, calibration-in-the-large, ECE, and linear-probability clipping counts distinguish probability-scale error from a proper-score increment.
hypotheses.H4_reused_data_limit: These strata reuse the already evaluated four L2 validation episodes. They can expose a boundary and freeze the next test, but they cannot independently confirm an action-relative HIT signal or identify a causal action effect.

non_goals: no Wine run, new collection, corpus mutation, refit, calibration transform, policy, critic, reward, OPE, IQL, history, MLP, or object encoder
no counterfactual successor and no claim that published-equals-baseline identifies the latent 80/20 mixture component
propensity, baseline identity, run identity, and time-since-HIT are diagnostic facts only and may not become actor inputs
physical HIT remains the only cost; post-HIT rows remain ordinary nonterminal portions of the complete episode
no threshold or stratum result from this reused corpus can promote a learner
